summary: The article provides largely accurate and well-supported advice for salaried taxpayers regarding ITR filing for FY26, emphasizing the importance of waiting for Form 16 and updated AIS/TIS. However, there are some inaccuracies regarding the revised return deadline and the replacement of Form 16.

claims.claim: The Income-Tax Department has released ITR forms for the Financial Year 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27).
claims.note: The Income Tax Department released Excel utilities and enabled online filing for ITR-1 and ITR-4 for AY 2026-27 in May 2026.

claims.claim: Your employer, for instance, has a deadline of June 15 to issue your Form 16, which is a crucial document detailing your salary, allowances, and the tax deducted at source (TDS).
claims.note: Employers are mandated to issue Form 16 for FY 2025-26 by June 15, 2026.

claims.claim: According to the Income Tax Act, employers must issue Form 16 by June 15 of the assessment year (for FY26, this means June 15, 2026). This statutory deadline is a key reason why waiting is prudent.
claims.note: Rule 31(3) of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, states that Form 16 must be furnished by June 15 of the financial year immediately following the financial year in which income was paid and tax deducted.

claims.claim: You must file the revised return before the end of the assessment year (i.e., by March 31, 2027, for FY26) or before the completion of the assessment, whichever is earlier.
claims.note: For AY 2026-27, a revised return under Section 139(5) can be filed on or before December 31, 2026, or before the completion of the assessment, whichever is earlier. While Budget 2026 proposed extending this to March 31 with late fees, the current rule for AY 2026-27 under the Income Tax Act, 1961, is December 31, 2026.

claims.claim: For income up to ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹1,000. For income above ₹5 lakhs, the fee is ₹5,000.
claims.note: For FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), the late filing fee under Section 234F is ₹1,000 for income up to ₹5 lakh and ₹5,000 for income exceeding ₹5 lakh.

claims.claim: The Income Tax Act provides for a penalty for misreporting of income. If the under-reported income is due to misreporting, a penalty of 50% of the tax payable on such under-reported income may be levied. In cases of "misreporting due to misrepresentation or suppression of facts," the penalty can go up to 200% of the tax payable on such under-reported income.
claims.note: Under Section 270A, the penalty for under-reporting income is 50% of the tax payable on such income, and for misreporting of income, it can be 200% of the tax payable on such income.

claims.claim: Form 16 is being replaced by Form 130 under the new Income Tax Act, 2025, effective from Tax Year 2026-27 onwards.
claims.note: The Income Tax Act, 2025, which replaces the Income Tax Act, 1961, introduces Form 130 to replace Form 16, effective from Tax Year 2026-27 (April 1, 2026) onwards.

article_title: Why Salaried Taxpayers Should Wait to File ITR for FY26
